title: Model Catalog demo - Crestview Health
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Crestview Health through the Model Catalog: selecting open models, interpreting benchmark profiles, and using compatibility matrices to pick model variants for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments. Discussed Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization), console filters, and security considerations (KMS, audit logs, SOC2). Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, and a short benchmark pilot on an H100-backed Dedicated node.
action_items: Owner:Alex Monroe | Item:Send tailored pricing sheet + model catalog PDF | Due:2026-03-18
Owner:Samira Kapoor | Item:Share compatibility matrix (A100/H100, seq len perf) spreadsheet and sample benchmark script | Due:2026-03-17
Owner:Sofia Martinez (Crestview) | Item:Provide data residency and compliance requirements; confirm SOC2 gap list | Due:2026-03-20
next_steps: Schedule 1-week pilot on Dedicated H100 with sample dataset (Redwood to provision)
Share security pack (SAML, KMS, audit logs) and network diagram
Follow-up call to review pilot results and finalize pricing
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through our model catalog demo, show how you pick open models and read the benchmark profiles. um, quick intros?
00:07 Dr. Nina Patel (Crestview): Hi I'm Nina, CTO, focused on ML ops and privacy for PHI, we want low latency for triage workflows.
00:13 Marcus Lee (Crestview): Marcus here, platform lead, mainly interested in deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated) and cost.
00:18 Sofia Martinez (Crestview): Sofia, security, gonna ask about KMS, audits, SSO.
00:22 Samira (Redwood SE): Samira, I'll do the deep dive on compatibility and benchmarks, and show Optimize suggestions.
00:29 Alex: Cool. opening the model catalog now — link: https://redwood.ai/model-catalog (note: demo link). first, the selection workflow: filter by task, latency profile, and certs.
00:44 Samira: i'll pull up an example: LlamaX-16b-open, shows perf profile for A100 fp16, H100 int8 and 4-bit. p50/p95 numbers are here but remember perf varies by seq len.
01:02 Marcus: how do we read this matrix? what's the difference between the p95 reported and what we'd see in our traffic?
01:10 Samira: good q. the catalog shows lab benchmarks (single-request p95) and batch profiles. for live traffic we suggest running the benchmark script we provide — it simulates your seq length dist. also Optimize recommends batching thresholds.
01:25 Dr. Nina Patel: we have a bunch of short prompts (20-60 tokens) for triage, but occasionally 1-2 longer notes ~512. will that change model choice?
01:35 Samira: yes — sequence length distribution drives kernel selection and kv cache memory. in the compatibility matrix we flag which model variants are better for long context (eg LlamaX-70b-ctx and variants with extended-kv). also quantization behavior can differ: 4-bit quantized runs faster but sometimes has small quality delta.
01:52 Alex: worth noting we can route by policy: short prompt traffic to a cheaper 16b quantized variant, fallback to 70b on errors or for high-complexity requests. that helps cost/latency tradeoffs.
02:08 Marcus: what's the expected latency on H100 for a 16b quantized model at p95 for 40 tokens?
02:16 Samira: our lab p95 for LlamaX-16b int8 on H100 is ~85-120ms for 40 tokens single request — rough ballpark, your infra and seq len mix will affect it. on A100 it's slightly higher.
02:31 Marcus: and cost delta?
02:33 Alex: dedicated H100 nodes are higher infra cost but per-token inference cost can be lower due to throughput. we'll send a model-by-model cost estimate.
02:40 Sofia: security — do you support customer-managed KMS and audit logs?
02:44 Samira: yes, for Private/Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integrations, and full audit logs; hosted has encrypted-at-rest and customer tenancy controls — we'll attach the security deck.
02:55 Dr. Nina Patel: data residency — can we keep logs off Redwood or only in our VPC?
03:00 Alex: Private mode gives you a private control plane and VPC option, logs can be routed to your SIEM; we also support retention policies and redaction.
03:10 Samira: back to the catalog UI — filters include model size, family, verification level (redwood-verified, community), and best-use tags (chat, summarization, embeddings). you can export a compatibility matrix per model.
03:25 Alex: demoing the compatibility matrix now — columns: model variant, supported quant formats (fp16, int8, nf4), supported hardware (A100/H100, T4 for smaller), recommended batch sizes, and observed p50/p95 for canonical seq lengths.
03:40 Marcus: does the matrix include memory footprint / required GPU memory for cache?
03:44 Samira: yes there's an approximate KV cache and peak mem column. it's approximate because it depends on context length and kv caching policy.
03:53 Dr. Nina Patel: we need guarantees about regression monitoring — if quantizing causes hallucinations we can't accept that in production. how do you detect regressions?
04:03 Alex: we tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and evals; Redwood Optimize can run evaluation tracks and send regression alerts when performance deviates from baseline. you can define golden prompts.
04:15 Sofia: what about SSO / RBAC?
04:18 Samira: SAML SSO and SCIM are supported, RBAC with per-route permissions, and token-level auditing in the console.
04:27 Marcus: show us the API call for selecting a model variant dynamically at request time.
04:31 Samira: yep — example: POST /v1/generate with model: "llamax-16b-int8" or model_alias in routing policy. dynamic routing shown. (slight audio blip) sorry, little echo.
04:50 Alex: file share — i'll drop the model catalog PDF and sample benchmark script in the follow-up.
04:55 Dr. Nina Patel: about dedicated vs hosted: if we start hosted and then move to dedicated, how seamless is the migration?
05:02 Alex: same API and console, you can pin model versions and rollout policies. traffic routing rules ensure consistent behavior; we recommend a canary rollout from hosted to dedicated.
05:12 Samira: also, Optimize will recommend different batching/quant profiles when you switch hardware, because kernel selection differs.
05:20 Marcus: are there any open-source model compat differences — like some community models don't support certain attention optimizations?
05:26 Samira: yes — some community weights are missing fused kernels or have custom ops. the catalog notes compatibility flags. for those we either use fallback kernels (slower) or recommend an alternate verified variant.
05:40 Alex: question from our side — timeline for pilot?
05:43 Marcus: we want a pilot next week if possible, 1 week subset of triage traffic.
05:47 Samira: we can provision a Dedicated H100 test node for a week, run your sample prompts, and produce a benchmark report. will need network whitelist and legal OK.
05:56 Sofia: we'll need the security pack and a draft contract redlines before infra access.
06:01 Alex: understood, will send security pack + pricing.
06:05 Samira: quick walk through of Optimize — here's a recommendation card: for your workload (short prompts + occasional long), it suggests LlamaX-16b int8 for fast paths, turn on prefix cache for repeated triage templates, and set batch target to 6-8 for throughput bursts. it also suggests enabling nf4 quant on H100 if you need extra speed.
06:28 Marcus: how do we validate that quality doesn't drop with nf4?
06:31 Samira: we run automated evals on your golden prompt set and flag score regressions, plus a manual sample review. you get the eval report in console and can enable automatic rollbacks.
06:44 Dr. Nina Patel: any PCI / HIPAA controls called out?
06:48 Sofia: i'll add that to the questions but HIPAA is key for us.
06:51 Alex: we have customers running PHI on Private — we'll share a healthcare compliance checklist and examples of customers in similar regs.
06:59 Samira: also noting that embeddings models have separate perf profiles; we often recommend deduped smaller models for vector search to cut cost.
07:10 Marcus: ok, can you show the console filters to export a compatibility csv?
07:15 Samira: clicking export — this export includes model, variant, quant formats, recommended hw, batch sizes, p50/p95 for 16/128/512 token profiles. i'll attach the csv.
07:27 Alex: wrap up — recap next steps: pricing, security pack, compatibility matrix + benchmark script, schedule pilot.
07:35 Dr. Nina Patel: sounds good. we'll review internally and Sofia will send the compliance list.
07:40 Marcus: thanks, appreciate the clear matrix view, that'll help our platform decision.
07:44 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD with materials.
07:47 (call ends)
